conventions.convention: Clamped degree-p knot vectors have endpoint multiplicity p+1 and nonempty B-spline supports. Interior multiplicity μ imposes matching through derivative order p−μ; C⁻¹ imposes no matching. Cells are left-closed and right-open, discontinuous knot values come from the right cell, and values at b are left limits. Zero-denominator recurrence terms are zero.

Natural cubic splines are C², piecewise cubic between at least two distinct knots, have zero second derivative at the extreme knots, and extend linearly on data-free tails. Repeated observations do not create additional knots.
The smoothing criterion uses λ>0, at least two distinct inputs, the continuous Sobolev representative for evaluations, and the squared L² norm of the second weak derivative. AC is assumed.

Local quasi-interpolants act on real continuous functions, reproduce P_l, and have common mesh-independent stability and neighborhood constants M and C_Q. Each neighborhood consists of at most M adjacent cells, and each point belongs to at most M neighborhoods.

Series least squares specifies the unique fitted training vector, even for rank-deficient designs; it does not select unique coefficients or assert independent test-risk control. Training prediction loss is n⁻¹ times squared Euclidean error against the target values at the training inputs.

The generic training-risk theorem uses iid observations, a supplied Borel conditional-law kernel, a supplied Borel conditional-mean version, a finite almost-everywhere conditional residual second-moment bound Δ, and a deterministic approximation coefficient vector. It makes no choice-based kernel-existence assertion.

The Sobolev training-rate corollary assumes AC and E|Y|<∞, imposes Sobolev smoothness on the selected regression version, uses an absolutely continuous design law with bounded density, and uses J uniform cells with full interior multiplicity p+1 and dimension K=(p+1)J.

load_bearing.statement: For the clamped knot convention, the degree-p B-splines are nonnegative, locally supported piecewise polynomials with the stated multiplicity-dependent regularity; the p+1 active functions on each nonempty knot interval form a basis of P_p and sum to one. Globally, the n B-splines form a basis of S_{p,ξ}, and every polynomial in P_p has a unique global expansion.

Assuming AC, a mesh-uniform bounded local quasi-interpolant reproducing P_l satisfies the local bound (1+C_Q)M^(l+1)h_m^(l+1)‖D^(l+1)f‖_{L^q(J_m)}/l! and the global bound (1+C_Q)M^(l+1+1/q)h^(l+1)‖D^(l+1)f‖_{L^q}/l!, for f∈W^(l+1,q), 0≤l≤p and 1≤q≤∞. On a full-multiplicity uniform mesh, the cellwise L² polynomial projector gives order h^s for integers 1≤s≤p+1.

Under the stated iid supplied-kernel conditional-mean model, conditional residual second moment at most Δ, and deterministic squared L²(P_X) approximation error at most C²K^(−2γ), the fitted training vector satisfies E[n⁻¹‖ĝ_K−g₀‖₂²]≤ΔK/n+C²K^(−2γ). This is expected empirical training-design loss.

For r≥2 distinct ordered knots in [a,b] and arbitrary real nodal values, there is exactly one natural cubic interpolant. Its interior nodal second derivatives solve the stated positive-definite tridiagonal system, its extreme second derivatives vanish, and it is linear outside the extreme knots.

Assuming AC, λ>0 and at least two distinct input values, the smoothing criterion J has a unique minimizer over W^{2,2}(a,b). It is the natural cubic spline at the distinct input values, with linear tails where needed.

concerns.concern: Verification 1.1 writes the cells as closed intervals [t_j,t_{j+1}] and claims the quasi-interpolant family has one-cell neighborhoods with M=1. The cited definition requires each point to belong to at most M neighborhoods. Closed adjacent cells share interior knots, so for J≥2 this particular convention gives overlap two, not one. Use the defining half-open cell convention, or state the corresponding overlap constant. The interpolation formula, stability estimate and direct h²/8 error proof remain sound.

alerts.finding: The Statement says “Let f:X→[0,+∞] be measurable and define ν_f(A):=∫_A f dμ (A∈𝒜). Then ν_f is a measure on (X,𝒜).” Its Given likewise specifies only “A nonnegative measurable function f.” Neither binds an ambient measure space (X,𝒜,μ), although the formula and proof require it. The proof is sound after that declaration; batch-27 consumer thm-series-training-risk, step 1.1, supplies the design product probability measure explicitly.

seams_checked.note: Checked both page summaries and the actual supplier/consumer interface. The series definition and training-risk proof use def-fixed-design-projection-estimator only for the unique realized-design fitted vector, retaining rank-deficient designs and making no coefficient-risk claim.

Checked both page summaries and def-regression-target-version against the Sobolev corollary. The corollary retains AC, E|Y|<∞, a selected conditional-law version, and an additional smoothness hypothesis. Its density assumption justifies replacing that version by its continuous Sobolev representative almost surely. The generic training theorem instead supplies its kernel and mean directly.
